title: Array sum n=5
question: Given an array of 5 integers, return the sum of all elements. Example: [-11, 5, -17, -16, 14] -> -25.
hints: Loop once and accumulate into a total starting at 0.
Empty array should return 0.
explanation:
Single pass accumulation is O(n) time, O(1) extra space.
---
Pattern guide: Arrays — indexed access, single pass first. Think in indices and windows: most array problems reduce to visiting each element once while carrying O(1) state. Recognize it when the input is ordered or indexable and the question asks for pairs, subarrays, or running totals. Canonical (verified): two_sum([2,7,11,15],9) -> [0,1] via a hash map of seen values — O(n) time, O(n) space. Traps: off-by-one on window edges; O(n^2) nested scans where a map or two pointers suffice. Transfers to: strings (as char arrays), sliding windows, prefix sums.

hints: Loop once and accumulate into a total starting at 0.
Empty array should return 0.
explanation:
Single pass accumulation is O(n) time, O(1) extra space.
---
Pattern guide: Arrays — indexed access, single pass first. Think in indices and windows: most array problems reduce to visiting each element once while carrying O(1) state. Recognize it when the input is ordered or indexable and the question asks for pairs, subarrays, or running totals. Canonical (verified): two_sum([2,7,11,15],9) -> [0,1] via a hash map of seen values — O(n) time, O(n) space. Traps: off-by-one on window edges; O(n^2) nested scans where a map or two pointers suffice. Transfers to: strings (as char arrays), sliding windows, prefix sums.

hints: Halve the range using the middle element each step.

explanation:

hints: Two pointers advance through the smaller head each step.
Append leftovers when one side exhausts.
explanation:
Two-pointer merge is O(n+m).
---
Pattern guide: Two pointers — sorted order is leverage. When sorted, the pair sum tells you which end to move: too big, shrink right; too small, grow left. Recognize it for pairs/triples in sorted arrays and in-place partition. Canonical (verified): pair summing to 6 in [1,2,3,4,6] -> indices [1,3] — O(n) time, O(1) space. Traps: forgetting to sort first; moving the wrong pointer; missing duplicates handling. Transfers to: binary search (same monotonicity instinct), palindromes, container problems.

title: Array intersection 0
question: Return sorted unique common elements of [2, 10, 7, 4, 6] and [10, 2, 10, 10, 7]. -> [2, 7, 10].

solution.code:
def intersection(a, b):
    return sorted(set(a) & set(b))

hints: A set gives O(1) membership tests.
Sort only for deterministic output.
explanation:
Set intersection is O(n+m) average.
---
Pattern guide: Hashing — trade space for lookups. Store what you have seen to answer 'have I met this before?' in O(1). Recognize it for duplicates, complements, frequencies. Canonical (verified): first duplicate of [2,5,1,2,3,5] -> 2 via a seen-set — O(n) time. Traps: unhashable types (lists/dicts as keys); relying on iteration order; hash collisions as a correctness (not just speed) issue in adversarial settings. Transfers to: two-sum, anagrams, sliding-window distinct counts.

title: Kth smallest k=4
question: Return 4th smallest of [16, 3, 30, 24, 18]. -> 24.

solution.code:
def kth(a, k):
    return sorted(a)[k - 1]

hints: Sort-then-index is simplest; heaps do it in O(n log k).
k is 1-indexed here.
explanation:
Sorting approach is O(n log n).
---

Pattern guide: SQL filtering — WHERE before grouping, HAVING after. WHERE filters rows before aggregation; HAVING filters groups after.
